title: Pretraining Data: What Models Learn From
summary: A pretrained model is a compressed summary of its training corpus. This lesson follows the data from raw web crawl to training tokens: the objective it is used for, how sources are mixed, how it is filtered and deduplicated, and how much of it a model of a given size needs.
objectives: Write the next-token cross-entropy objective over a corpus and compute it and its perplexity for a short sequence
Turn mixture weights and source sizes into tokens drawn and epochs per source
Compute Jaccard similarity on shingles and explain why MinHash with banding finds near-duplicates cheaply
Compare models by tokens per parameter and estimate a corpus size in tokens from bytes
Detect and reason about benchmark contamination with n-gram overlap
prerequisites: You should know what a token is ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)) and what cross-entropy loss measures ([How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn)). Log-probabilities and perplexity are introduced in [Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling); they are re-derived here, so that lesson helps but is not required.
